Diagnosis Comments:
The tumor consists of a hypercellular population of glial cells with admixed variably sized neurons. These neurons are present in small groups and clusters with architectural disarray and mild pleomorphism. These cells are especially predominant around vascular structures. Occasional eosinophilic granular bodies are noted. The grading of gangliogliomas is subjective, but the tumors that resemble dysplastic processes rather than proliferative tumors are more likely to be classified as WHO Grade I lesions, while tumors that exhibit a more diffuse growth pattern and multifocality are more likely to be considered WHO Grade II. The prognostic significance of Grade I vs. Grade II gangliogliomas is not well established.
Immunohistochemical studies were performed and evaluated in our laboratory on blocks A2 and C7 to confirm the final diagnosis. The studies show that the abnormal neuronal cells are positive with antibodies against Neu-N, as well as CD34, confirming the nature and extent of this glioneuronal tumor. Immunohistochemical staining for ki-67 (MIB-1) antibody demonstrates a low labeling index. These findings confirm the diagnosis of ganglioglioma.

COMMENT:  
Sections demonstrate a solid appearing neoplasm composed of atypical
glial cells and dysmorphic ganglion cells. Mitoses are inconspicuous,
and no microvascular proliferation or necrosis is seen. To further
evaluate the tumor cells, immunohistochemical stains were performed and
evaluated on block C1 and are interpreted as follows:
Synaptophysin:  Positive in neoplastic ganglion cell component. 
NeuN:  Neoplastic ganglion cells show diminished weak staining.
Reticulin:  Shows increased intercellular reticulin deposition.
p16:  Strongly positive in tumor cells. 
BRAF V600E:  Positive for mutant protein. 
ATRX:  Intact/retained expression, with variable intensity.
Ki-67:  Labeling index estimated at approximately 4% in tumor cells
(also highlights admixed lymphocytes).
The morphologic and immunohistochemical findings support the diagnosis
of residual/recurrent ganglioglioma, WHO grade I.  This ganglioglioma
demonstrates abundant intercellular reticulin deposition, which is an
unusual feature for gangliogliomas and similar cases have sometimes been
referred to in the literature as non-infantile desmoplastic
ganglioglioma.  The intact p16 expression, definitive ganglion cell
component, and absence of xanthomatous cells all argue against the
alternative possibility of pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma.  This
residual/recurrent ganglioglioma will also be evaluated using the
USC500 NGS panel for further genetic characterization and the results
will be reported separately, as well as in an addendum if clinically
indicated.
